text.p: The American Bar Association, the world's largest legal group, will consider condemning a practice by bond lawyers making political contributions to municipal officials to influence the award of government bond work.
The group's policy making body will vote on the proposal condemning the practice called "pay to play" during the ABA's annual meeting in San Francisco. The meeting runs from July 31 to Aug. 6.
The proposal also requests the ABA president to appoint a task force to study the issues related to the practice and suggest possible solutions.
The Association of the Bar of the City of New York, which presented the proposal to the ABA, also suggested a ban on "pay to play" to New York State officials earlier this year.
